content_paraphrased: Infer properties of populations or distributions from a sample, while knowing the limitations of sampling
teaching: Biased samples; estimating a population from a random sample
gap: Designing a sampling method is chosen from options; not written

content_paraphrased: Interpret and construct tables, charts and diagrams, including frequency tables, bar charts, pie charts and pictograms for categorical data, vertical line charts for ungrouped discrete numerical data, tables and line graphs for time series data; know their appropriate use
teaching: Reading bar charts; pie chart angles and back to frequencies
gap: Constructing (drawing) charts is not marked; pictograms, vertical line charts and time series graphs are taught in the cards only, not generated as practice

content_paraphrased: Construct and interpret diagrams for grouped discrete data and continuous data, i.e. histograms with equal and unequal class intervals and cumulative frequency graphs, and know their appropriate use
teaching: Frequency density; reading cumulative frequency graphs
gap: Drawing histograms and cumulative frequency graphs is not marked; values are read from drawn graphs

content_paraphrased: Interpret, analyse and compare the distributions of data sets from univariate empirical distributions through: appropriate graphical representation involving discrete, continuous and grouped data, including box plots (H); appropriate measures of central tendency (median, mean, mode and modal class) and spread (range, including consideration of outliers, quartiles and inter-quartile range (H))
teaching: Mean, median, mode, range from lists and tables; comparing distributions; Higher: quartiles, IQR, box plots
gap: Drawing box plots is not marked

content_paraphrased: Apply statistics to describe a population
teaching: Choosing an average; comparing two groups in context
gap: Written comparisons are chosen from options

content_paraphrased: Use and interpret scatter graphs of bivariate data; recognise correlation and know that it does not indicate causation; draw estimated lines of best fit; make predictions; interpolate and extrapolate apparent trends while knowing the dangers of so doing
teaching: Correlation types; predictions; outliers; causation; extrapolation
gap: Drawing a line of best fit is chosen from three lines in the investigation; not freehand
